acceptance.criterion_verbatim: RESIDUAL ENUM IS MECE -- mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive (Rule 24(i)), at ONE grain (24(ii)), serving ONE intent (24(iii)), with the stability frame named (24(iv): say which values move together under one remedy and which do not).
acceptance.invocation: yaml.safe_load over data/_contracts/smartx_bd_join_disposition.yaml + arithmetic check of sum(measured) vs the printed denominator
acceptance.output_evidence: ALL FOUR POSTULATES SATISFIED AND EACH IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN ASSERTED. (i) MECE: values JOINED 7286 + KEY_OUTSIDE_ACCOUNT_GRAMMAR 16 + KEY_VALID_ACCOUNT_ABSENT 3 + UNRESOLVED 0 = 7305 = the printed denominator, verified arithmetically by machine (yaml load + sum == denominator -> True); the tests are structurally disjoint (an 8-digit key cannot also be a non-8-digit key; present cannot also be absent), so mutual exclusivity is by construction, not by convention. (ii) ONE GRAIN: every value is a property of ONE ALLOCATION MAP ROW (allocation_id x as_of); declared in the contract's axis.grain. (iii) ONE INTENT: JOIN-RESOLUTION OUTCOME ONLY -- explicitly not cause, lifecycle, custody, or attribute provenance. (iv) STABILITY FRAME NAMED, AND IT SPLITS: KEY_VALID_ACCOUNT_ABSENT moves under an account-universe refresh; KEY_OUTSIDE_ACCOUNT_GRAMMAR does NOT move under ANY refresh (no refresh of a universe of zfilled 8-digit ids can admit a 9-digit key) -- its remedy is a scope decision with a different owner. Consequence stated: a 'refresh the dimension' plan covers 3 of 19 rows and structurally cannot reach the other 16. FOUR PRD-PROPOSED VALUES WERE REJECTED ON MEASURED GROUNDS, not preference: NO_SMARTX_ALLOCATION (wrong grain -- account-grain, measured separately at 1,575/7,316), CLOSED (mixes lifecycle with outcome AND classifies nothing -- the map holds zero 'close' rows, all 19 residuals are 'open', all 26 'workingClose' joined), OTHER_CUSTODIAN (a cause, and INFERRED -- nothing names a custodian), plus two renames (NON_8DIGIT_KEY named the test not the outcome; NOT_IN_ACCOUNT_UNIVERSE was ambiguous across both residual classes).
acceptance.denominator: 7,305 allocation map rows; 4 retained values + 5 dispositioned proposals = 9 values adjudicated

mutant.description: The residual classification's central risk is that the \d{8} filter MANUFACTURES the residual it reports -- i.e. that the 16 excluded rows are resolvable and the instrument is hiding them. That is the exact 'unresolvable vs resolvable-but-in-the-residual' confusion CTO named as the reason D6/TO-G gates on this enum, so I attacked it directly rather than trusting the class. THREE CONTROLS RUN: (1) RELAXED-JOIN -- drop the 8-digit constraint, zfill the 13 distinct 9-digit keys to 10, test universe membership. (2) POSITIVE -- run 50 known 8-digit keys through the SAME membership test. (3) UNIVERSE SHAPE -- census the id length and leading characters of the whole universe.
mutant.expected: if the filter were manufacturing residual, the relaxed join would find hits; a working membership test must find the known-good keys; and the universe must be shown to be incapable of containing a 9-digit id rather than merely observed not to.
mutant.observed: (1) 0 of 13 relaxed-join hits -- the 9-digit keys are genuinely absent, not filtered out. (2) 50 of 50 known 8-digit keys FOUND, so the membership test discriminates and the zero in (1) is specific rather than global. (3) 7,316 of 7,316 universe ids are 10-char and '00'-leading, i.e. exclusively zfilled 8-digit -- ZERO native 9/10-digit members, so the exclusion is STRUCTURAL. A synthetic negative control (9999999999) was also absent, confirming the test is not undiscriminating. All three agree: KEY_OUTSIDE_ACCOUNT_GRAMMAR is a real class, not an artifact.
